name: Proverbs
sourceNote: Written freshly, thought for thought, from the oldest Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic witnesses (the Masoretic Text with the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Septuagint, and the Samaritan Pentateuch). © 2026 Jose Santiago. All rights reserved.

verses.text: Here are the wise sayings{a} of Solomon,{b} who was David’s{c} son and ruled Israel.{d}

They are written so you can learn wisdom and self-control
and understand deep and helpful words.

They teach you how to be sensible,
honest, fair, and just.

They give clear thinking to people who are easily fooled,
and knowledge and good judgment to the young.

Wise people who listen will learn even more.
Those with understanding will gain the skill of good guidance.

They will make sense of sayings and word pictures,
and of the teachings and puzzles of wise people.

Respect for Yahweh is where knowledge starts.{e}
Fools look down on wisdom and correction.{f}

My child, pay attention when your father trains you.
Never toss aside your mother’s teaching.{g}

Their teaching will be like a beautiful wreath on your head,
and like a necklace around your neck.

My child, sinners may try to lure you along.
Say no to them.

They may say, “Join us!
We will hide and wait to kill someone.
We will jump on an innocent person just for fun.

We will swallow them whole, like the grave,{h}
healthy and strong, like people dropping into a pit.

We will find all kinds of valuable things.
We will pack our houses with stolen goods.

Throw in your lot with us.
We will all share one purse.”

My child, do not walk down that road with them.
Keep your feet off their path.

Their feet hurry toward harm.
They rush to spill blood.
A bird will not land where a net is spread out in plain sight.{i}

But these men are really setting an ambush for themselves.
They are hiding to catch their own lives.

That is where greed leads every time.
It takes the life of the person who holds on to it.

Out in the street Wisdom{j} calls aloud.
In the open squares her voice rings out.

From the top of the noisy walls she shouts.
Right where the city gates open, she gives her speech:

“How long will you simple people keep loving your simple ways?
How long will mockers enjoy mocking,
and fools keep hating knowledge?

Turn back when I warn you!
Then I will pour out my spirit on you
and share my words with you.

I called, but you refused to come.
I reached out my hand, and no one cared.

You ignored all my advice.
You did not want my correction.

So I will laugh at your trouble when it hits.
I will tease you when terror comes.

Terror will sweep over you like a windstorm.
Disaster will rush in like a whirling storm.
Pain and misery will pile up on you.

Then you will cry out to me, but I will give no answer.
You will hunt for me, yet you will not find me.

You hated knowledge.
You did not choose to respect Yahweh.

You refused my guidance.
You brushed off all my corrections.

So you will eat what your own choices grew.
You will be stuffed with your own plans.

Simple people die because they wander off.
Fools are destroyed by their own comfort.

But whoever listens to me will rest safely.
They will be calm and not afraid of harm.”

notes.text: The Hebrew word mishle means proverbs, wise sayings, comparisons, and short stories with a lesson.
Solomon means “peaceful” (it is related to shalom, “peace”).
David means “beloved.”
Israel means “he struggles with God” (Genesis 32:28).
Or “the main part of knowledge.”
The Septuagint adds a line: “There is good understanding for everyone who practices it. Respect for God is the start of seeing clearly.”
The Hebrew word is torah, which means “teaching.” It later became the name of the Law.
Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead. The next line calls it “the pit.”
The point may be that even a bird is smart enough to avoid an obvious trap. Another view is that the bird sees only the food and is caught anyway.
In Hebrew, Wisdom is a plural word (chokhmoth). She speaks like a woman in public. She is seen again in chapters 8 and 9.

verses.text:
My child, suppose you accept what I say
and treasure my instructions deep inside.

Suppose you listen closely for wisdom
and set your mind on understanding.

Suppose you beg for good sense
and shout out for understanding.

Suppose you search for her as you would for silver
and dig for her like buried treasure.

Then you will come to respect Yahweh
and discover what it means to know God.

Yahweh is the one who gives wisdom.
Knowledge and understanding come out of his mouth.

He saves up success{a} for honest people.
He is a shield for those who live without blame.

He guards the paths of fairness
and watches over the road of his loyal people.{b}

Then you will see what is right, just, and fair,
and you will know every good path.

Wisdom will enter your heart,
and knowledge will make your soul glad.

Good judgment will watch over you.
Understanding will stand guard around you.

They will save you from the path of evil
and from men who twist the truth when they talk.

These men leave the straight roads
to walk in dark paths.

They enjoy doing wrong.
They cheer when evil turns things upside down.

Their roads wind and bend.
Their ways go off in crooked directions.

Wisdom will also rescue you from an outsider woman,{c}
a stranger who uses smooth words.

She has walked away from the husband of her youth.
She has forgotten the promise she made before her God.{d}

Her house sinks down toward death.{e}
Her paths go down to the spirits of the dead.{f}

None who visit her ever come home.
They never get back onto the paths of life.

So walk with good people.
Stay on the road that honest people travel.

Honest people will live in the land,
and those without blame will stay there.

But the wicked will be removed from the earth,
and the unfaithful will be pulled out of it like weeds.

notes.text: The Hebrew word tushiyyah can mean “success” or “sound judgment.”
Hebrew chasidim, people who are loyal to God’s promise.
Hebrew zarah, “stranger,” and nokhriyyah, “foreigner.” In Proverbs these words describe a married woman who is unfaithful to her husband. She appears again in 5:3–20, 6:24–35, and 7:5–27.
Or “the promise made in the presence of her God,” meaning her wedding vow.
Or “She herself sinks down to death, and her house with her.” The Hebrew is hard to read.
Hebrew repha’im, the spirits of the dead in Sheol.

verses.text:
My child, never forget what I teach.
Let your heart hold on to my commands.

They will give you more days to live,
more years, and a peaceful life.

Never let kindness and truth walk away from you.
Wear them like a chain on your neck.
Carve them on the tablet of your heart.

Then God and people
will think well of you and respect you.

Trust Yahweh completely.
Do not lean on what you understand yourself.

Include him in everything you do,
and he will make your paths straight.

Do not think you are wise by yourself.
Respect Yahweh and stay away from evil.

It will heal your body{a}
and refresh your bones.{b}

Honor Yahweh with your wealth,
with the first part of everything you harvest.

Then your barns will overflow,
and your jars will spill over with fresh wine.

My child, do not turn away when Yahweh trains you.
Do not get upset when he corrects you.

Yahweh corrects the ones he loves,
the way a father corrects a son who makes him proud.{c}

How happy is the person who finds wisdom,
who gains understanding!

Wisdom earns more than silver does.
Her gain is better than pure gold.

She is worth more than jewels.{d}
Nothing you could want is as good as she is.

A long life is in her right hand.
Wealth and honor are in her left.{e}

Her roads are pleasant,
and every path she takes leads to peace.

She is a tree of life for those who grab hold of her.
Everyone who keeps her close is blessed.

Yahweh used wisdom to lay the foundations of the earth.
He used understanding to set the sky above.

His knowledge split open the deep waters
and let the clouds drop their dew.

My child, keep your eyes on these things.
Hold on to good sense and sound judgment.

They will give life to your soul
and make a lovely chain for your neck.

You will walk safely on your way,
and you will not stub your toe.

When you lie down, you will not be afraid.
You will rest and sleep well.{f}

Do not be afraid of sudden danger,
or of the crash that hits the wicked.

Yahweh will be the one you can count on.
He will keep your foot out of the trap.

Do not keep back good things from people who have earned them,
when you have the power to give.

Do not tell your neighbor, “Go away and return later.
I will give it tomorrow,” when you already have it.

Do not plan to hurt your neighbor
while he lives next door and trusts you.

Do not start a fight with someone for no reason
when he has done you no harm.

Do not envy a violent man.
Do not pick any of his ways to copy.

Yahweh hates those who are dishonest,
but he shares his secrets with honest people.

Yahweh’s curse rests on the home of wicked people,
but he blesses the house of those who do right.

He laughs at proud mockers,
yet he is kind to the humble.{g}

Wise people will receive honor,
but fools will be rewarded with shame.{h}

notes.text: Or “your belly button.” The Septuagint reads “your body.”
Literally, “a drink for your bones.”
The Septuagint says “he whips every child he accepts.” This is the form quoted in Hebrews 12:6.
Or “rubies” or “pearls.” The exact stone is not certain.
The Septuagint adds, “Right living comes out of her mouth. She carries law and mercy on her tongue.”
The Septuagint says, “If you rest, you will not be afraid. If you sleep, your sleep will be sweet.”

The Septuagint says, “The Lord stands against the proud but gives kindness to the humble.” This is the form quoted in James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5. The Greek word kyrios (“Lord”) usually stands for Yahweh.
Or “but fools lift up shame.” The Hebrew is uncertain.

subheads.13: Wisdom Is Worth More Than Gold

verses.text:
Children, hear your father’s training.
Pay attention and gain understanding.

The lesson I give you is a good one.
Do not turn your back on what I teach.

I was once a boy in my own father’s house.
I was small, and my mother’s only son.

My father taught me and said,
“Hold my words tightly in your heart.
Obey my commands and you will live.

Get wisdom. Get understanding.
Do not forget my words, and do not wander from them.

Stay with wisdom, and she will keep you safe.
Care for her deeply, and she will guard you.

Wisdom comes first, so get wisdom!
Whatever else you get, get understanding.{a}

Hold her in high value, and she will raise you up.
Wrap your arms around her, and she will bring you honor.

She will crown you with a lovely wreath.
She will give you a glorious crown.”

Listen, my child, and accept my words.
Then you will live many years.

I have shown you the road of wisdom.
I have led you down straight paths.

When you walk, nothing will hold you back.
When you run, you will not fall.

Grab hold of instruction and never let it go.
Keep it carefully, for it is your life.

Do not step onto the path of wicked people.
Do not walk down the road of those who do evil.

Stay away from it. Do not go near.
Turn around and go the other way.

They cannot sleep until they have done something bad.
They lie awake until they have made someone stumble.

Wickedness is the bread they eat.
Violence is the wine they drink.

The path of good people is like the early morning light.
It grows brighter until the day is full.

Wicked people travel in thick darkness.
They cannot see what they trip over.

My child, give attention to my words.
Bend your ear toward what I say.

Never lose sight of them.
Hold them in the middle of your heart.

They give life to anyone who finds them
and health to the whole body.

Above all else, protect your heart,
because your whole life flows from it.

Keep lying words out of your mouth.
Keep twisted talk far from your lips.

Look straight ahead.
Keep your eyes fixed on what is in front of you.

Make a smooth path for your feet.
Then every road you take will be safe.

Do not veer to either side.
Keep your feet from evil.{b}

notes.text: This verse is not in the Septuagint.
The Septuagint adds, “God knows the roads on the right, but the ones on the left are crooked. He will straighten your paths and lead you in peace.”

verses.text:
My child, tune in to my wisdom.
Lean close to hear my understanding.

Then you will keep your good judgment,
and your lips will guard what you know.

Honey drips from the lips of a faithless woman.
Her talk is silkier than oil.

In the end, though, she tastes as bitter as wormwood.{a}
She cuts like a sword with two sharp edges.

Her feet go down into death.
Every step she takes ends at the grave.

Life’s path never crosses her mind.
Her roads twist about, though she cannot tell.{b}

So now, my children, hear me out.
Never walk away from what I say.

Keep far away from her road.
Do not even go near her door.

If you do, you may give your best years to others,
and the rest of your life to someone cruel.

Strangers will take what your strength has earned.
Your hard work will fill another person’s house.

At the end of your life you will groan,
when your body is worn out.

You will say, “I hated being corrected!
My heart refused every warning.

I would not obey my teachers.
I never tilted my ear to those who trained me.

I nearly lost everything
in front of the whole community.”

Drink from your own well.
Let fresh water flow from your own spring.{c}

Why should your streams pour out into the streets?
Why should your fresh water run through the town squares?

Keep it for yourself.
Do not share it with strangers.

May your own fountain bring you a blessing.
Be glad over the bride of your younger days.

She is a charming deer, a graceful mountain goat.
Let her love satisfy you at all times.
Let her love keep you spellbound.

My child, why let a stranger’s wife dazzle you?
Why hold in your arms a woman who is not yours?

Yahweh sees every move a person makes.
He studies{d} every path.

The sins of wicked people trap them.
The ropes of their own wrongs hold them tight.

They die because they would not learn.
Their huge foolishness makes them stumble away.{e}

notes.text: Wormwood is a plant with a very bitter taste. People used it as a picture of bitterness.
Or “She makes sure you do not walk on the level path of life. Her roads wander, and you do not know it.”
In verses 15–18 the water, well, and fountain stand for a man’s own wife.
Or “measures.”
The Hebrew word for “stumble away” also means “be drunk.” It is the same word used in verses 19 and 20.

subheads.15: Be Happy with Your Own Wife

verses.text:
My child, you may have promised to pay a neighbor’s debt.
You may have shaken hands on a loan for a stranger.

If your own words have trapped you,
and your own lips have caught you,

here is what to do to get free, my child.
You are in your neighbor’s power,
so go and beg{a} him without stopping.

Do not let yourself sleep.
Do not let your eyes close.

Slip out like a deer escaping a hunter,{b}
like a bird getting away from a trapper.

Lazy person, visit the ants.
Watch what they do and learn.

They have no chief.
They have no boss or ruler.

Still, they store up food in the summer
and collect their supplies at harvest time.{c}

Lazy person, how long will you stay in bed?
When will you get up?

A short nap, a little rest,
a quick fold of the arms to relax,

and then poverty will arrive like a robber,
and need will come like a man with a weapon.{d}

A worthless person,{e} a troublemaker,
goes around speaking lies.

He winks with one eye, taps with his foot,
and points with his finger.

His heart is twisted. He is always planning something bad.
He keeps starting arguments.

So disaster will hit him without warning.
He will be smashed in a moment, and no one can fix him.

Yahweh hates six things.
Seven things are disgusting to him:{f}

proud looks, a lying tongue,
hands that kill innocent people,

a heart that plans evil,
feet that hurry to do wrong,

a witness who tells lies with every breath,
and anyone who starts fights among family.

My child, obey the command of your father.
Do not throw away your mother’s teaching.

Tie them to your heart for good.
Fasten them around your neck.

As you walk, they will lead you.
As you sleep, they will keep guard.
At dawn they will talk with you.

The command is a lamp, and the teaching is a light.
Correction that trains you is the road to life.

They will keep you away from an evil woman,{g}
away from the slippery words of a stranger.

Never long for her looks in your heart.
Never let her glances snare you.

A woman who sells herself may cost a single loaf.
A married woman, though, goes after a man’s whole life.{h}

Can anyone carry fire in the lap of his robe
without burning his clothes?

Can anyone step on burning coals
and keep his feet unhurt?

It is the same for the man who sleeps with his neighbor’s wife.
Whoever touches her will pay for it.

People do not hate a thief for stealing
when he is starving and needs food.

When he is found out, he owes seven times the loss.
He could lose all that his family owns.

Anyone who sleeps with another man’s wife lacks sense.
He wrecks himself.

He will get wounds and shame.
His disgrace will never be erased.

A husband’s jealousy burns with anger.
He will show no mercy on the day he takes revenge.

No payment will satisfy him.
He will turn down your gifts, however large.

notes.text: Or “crush your pride and beg.”
The Hebrew says “from the hand.” The words “of a hunter” come from the matching line and some old copies.

The Septuagint adds, “Or go to the bee and see how hard she works. Kings and ordinary people use what she makes to stay healthy. Everyone wants it and honors her. She is weak, yet she is respected because she values wisdom.”
The Septuagint adds, “But if you work hard, your harvest will arrive like a spring of water, and poverty will run away like a poor runner.”
Hebrew adam beliyya’al, “a man of Belial.” Belial means worthless or wicked.
This is a “six, then seven” saying. A similar pattern appears in 30:15–31.
The Septuagint says “a married woman.”
Or “For because of a woman who sells herself, a man is reduced to a loaf of bread.” This line is hard to read in Hebrew.

verses.text:
My child, hold on to what I say.
Store my commands up inside you.{a}

Follow my commands and you will live.
Protect my teaching like the apple of your eye.

Wrap them around your fingers.
Write them on the tablet of your heart.

Tell wisdom, “You are my sister.”
Call understanding your close friend.

They will keep you away from an unfaithful woman,
from the stranger with her smooth words.

Once I stood at the window of my house
and looked out through the shutters.

I spotted a group of simple people.
Among the young men I noticed one
who had no sense.

He was walking down the street near her corner,
heading for her house.

It was twilight, as the day was ending,
in the black of night.

A woman came out to meet him.
Her clothes were those of a woman who sells herself, and her plans were secret.{b}

She was loud and wild.
Her feet would not stay home.

One minute she was in the street, the next in the market.
At every corner she lay in wait.

She grabbed him and kissed him.
Without shame she told him,

“I owed peace offerings,
and today I kept my promises.{c}

So I came out to find you.
I looked for you everywhere, and here you are!

I put fresh covers on my bed,
bright cloth from Egypt.

I have perfumed my bed
with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

Come, let us enjoy love until morning.
Let us have fun together.

My husband is away from home.
His trip will take him far.

He took a bag of coins along.
He plans to return at full moon.”

With so much talk she turned him her way.
With her smooth lips she pushed him along.

Soon an arrow would strike deep inside him.
He was a bird flying into a snare.
He never guessed that his life was on the line.

So now, my children, listen to me.
Hear every word I say.

Do not let your heart drift toward her roads.
Do not wander onto her paths.

She has brought down many victims.
Her list of dead men is long.

Her house leads down to the grave.
Its halls end in the rooms of death.

notes.text: The Septuagint adds two lines: “My child, honor the Lord and you will be strong. Fear no one but him.”
Or “with a secret purpose” or “with a covered heart.”
The meat from a peace offering had to be eaten within a day or two (Leviticus 7:15–16). So she has food ready.
The Hebrew of this line is not certain. The Septuagint says, “like a dog into chains, or like a deer shot in the body with an arrow.”

subheads.6: A Young Man and a Dangerous Woman

verses.text:
Can you hear that? Wisdom is calling out.
Understanding is raising her voice.{a}

She takes her place on the hills beside the road,
where the paths cross.

Next to the gates that lead into town,
right at the doorways, she shouts:

“People, I am calling to you.
My voice reaches every human being.

Simple people, learn to be sharp.
Fools, get some sense.{b}

Listen, because what I say is noble.
My lips speak what is right.

My mouth tells the truth.
My lips cannot stand evil.

Every word I speak is fair.
None of it is bent or twisted.

To people with understanding, it is all clear.
To those who have found knowledge, it is correct.

Choose my teaching over silver.
Choose knowledge over the finest gold.

Wisdom is worth more than jewels.
No treasure can match her.

I, Wisdom, live next door to good sense.
I am the one who finds knowledge and good judgment.

To respect Yahweh is to hate evil.
I hate pride, bragging, wicked ways,
and twisted talk.

Advice and sound thinking belong to me.
I am understanding, and I have power.

Kings rule because of me.
Rulers make fair laws with my help.

Princes lead with my help,
and so do all the noble judges of the world.{c}

I love those who love me.
Anyone who searches for me eagerly will find me.

Wealth and honor are mine to give,
along with lasting riches and right living.

What I give is better than gold, even fine gold.
What I earn beats the best silver.

I walk down the road of what is right,
along the middle of the paths of justice.

I give wealth to those who love me,
and I fill up their storehouses.{d}

Yahweh made me{e} at the very start of his work,
before anything else he did long ago.

I was set in place ages ago,{f}
at the beginning, before the earth existed.

I was born when no deep seas existed,
when no springs overflowed with water.

Before the mountains sank into place,
before any hills, I was born.

He had not made the land, the open country,
or even the first bit of soil.

I was present as he fixed the heavens above,
as he drew a circle over the face of the deep.

I was there when he made the clouds solid above,
when he made the springs of the deep flow strong.

I was there when he gave the sea its edge,
so its waters would not go past his command,
and when he marked out the foundations of the earth.

I played over his world, the earth,
and I found my joy in human beings.

Now, my children, pay attention.
Happy are those who stay on my paths.

Listen to this teaching, and become wise.
Never brush it aside.

Happy is the person who hears me,
who waits at my gates every day,
who stands guard at my doorposts.

Whoever finds me finds life,
and wins Yahweh’s approval.

But anyone who misses me hurts himself.{h}
Everyone who hates me loves death instead.”

notes.text: Wisdom speaks for herself in this whole chapter. See the note at 1:20 about her.
Literally “understand a heart.”
Literally “all judges of righteousness.” The Septuagint and some other old copies say “of the earth.”
The Septuagint adds, “If I tell you what happens each day, I will remember to tell about things from long ago.”

Hebrew qanani, from qanah. This word usually means “get” or “own” (see 4:5 and 4:7). In a few places it may mean “create” or “give birth to” (Genesis 14:19, 22; Deuteronomy 32:6). The Septuagint says “created me.”
Or “woven together” (compare Psalm 139:13), or “put in office.”
Hebrew amon. Another reading, amun, means “a little child being raised.” The Septuagint says “fitting myself to him.”
Or “anyone who sins against me.”

verses.text:
Wisdom has built a house for herself.
She has cut out seven pillars for it.{a}

She has prepared meat, mixed her wine,
and laid out her table.

She has sent her servant girls to call out
from the highest places in town:

“Whoever is simple, come on in!”
To those with no sense, she says,

“Come, eat my bread.
Drink the wine I have blended.

Give up your simple ways and live.
Walk on the road of understanding.”

Correct a mocker and you will get insults back.
Warn a wicked person and you will get hurt.

Do not scold a mocker, or he will hate you.
Scold a wise person, and he will love you for it.

Teach a wise person and he will grow wiser still.
Instruct a good person and he will learn more.

Respect for Yahweh is where wisdom begins.
Knowing the Holy One{b} is what understanding means.{c}

Because of wisdom, you will have many more days,
and years will be added to your life.

If you are wise, you gain from it yourself.
If you are a mocker, you alone pay the price.{d}

Lady Folly{e} is loud.
She is simple and knows nothing.

She sits at her own doorway.
She sits on a chair up on the town’s high ground.

She calls to everyone who passes by,
people who are minding their own business:

“Anyone who is simple, come in here!”
To those with no sense, she says,

“Stolen water tastes sweet.
Food eaten in secret is delicious.”

But the guest does not know the dead are there,
and her visitors are already in the deep places of the grave.{f}

notes.text: The seven pillars could mean a grand house, the seven days of creation, or the fullness of Wisdom’s work. People disagree.
Hebrew qedoshim, a plural word. It may be a plural of greatness, or it may mean “holy ones.”
The Septuagint adds, “To know the law is the sign of a healthy mind.”

The Septuagint adds three verses. They say that trusting in lies is like herding the wind and chasing flying birds, or like leaving your own vineyard and walking through a dry desert, picking up nothing with your hands.

Literally “a woman of folly.” Folly is shown as a rival of Wisdom who invites the same guests (compare verses 4 and 16). The second line is uncertain. The Septuagint says, “and she does not know shame.”

The Septuagint adds, “Hurry away. Do not wait there or fix your eyes on her. If you do, you will cross over strange water. Stay away from strange water. Do not drink from a strange spring. Then you will live long, and years will be added to your life.”

verses.text:
Treasure won by crime does no good,
but doing right saves a life from death.

Yahweh does not let good people starve,
but he blocks the greedy hopes of the wicked.

Lazy hands bring poverty,
but busy hands bring wealth.{b}

Gathering crops in summer is the act of a wise child.
Sleeping through harvest is the act of a child who shames the family.

Blessings crown the heads of good people,
but violence hides behind the words of the wicked.{c}

The memory of a good person is a blessing,
but the name of a wicked person rots away.

A wise heart accepts orders,
but a fool who talks too much will fall flat.

Honest people walk without fear,
but people with crooked ways will be caught.

Whoever winks with an eye causes pain,
and a fool who talks too much will fall flat.{d}

The words of good people are a spring that gives life,
but violence hides behind the words of the wicked.

Hate starts fights,
but love covers over every wrong.

Wisdom shows up in the speech of people with understanding.
A stick is the right tool for the back of one who lacks sense.

Wise people save up what they learn,
but a fool’s mouth invites disaster.

The rich have wealth as their walled city.
The poor have poverty as their ruin.

What good people earn gives them life.
What the wicked earn leads them to sin.

Whoever accepts training walks the road to life.
Whoever turns down correction leads others off track.

A person who hides hate while smiling is a liar.
A person who spreads gossip is a fool.

Where there are many words, wrong is never far away.
Whoever keeps his mouth shut shows good sense.

What good people say is like pure silver.
The thoughts of the wicked are worth little.

The words of good people nourish many.
Fools die because they have no sense.

Yahweh’s blessing is what brings wealth,
and hard work adds nothing to it.{e}

A fool thinks doing wrong is fun,
but a person with understanding finds wisdom fun.

What the wicked dread comes true for them.
What the good long for is given to them.

After the storm blows past, the wicked are gone.
The good stand firm forever.

Vinegar hurts the teeth, and smoke stings the eyes.
A lazy messenger does the same to the one who sends him.

Respect for Yahweh adds days to life,
but the wicked have their years cut short.

The hope of good people ends in joy,
but the wicked see their hopes come to nothing.

Yahweh’s way is a fortress for honest people,
but it is ruin for those who do wrong.

Good people will never be shaken.
The wicked will not stay in the land.

The mouth of a good person grows wise words,
but a twisted tongue will be cut out.

The lips of a good person know what fits the moment,
but the mouth of the wicked knows nothing but crooked words.

notes.text: Chapters 10:1–22:16 are a collection of mostly two-line sayings. There are 375 of them. That matches the number value of the Hebrew letters in the name Solomon (shlmh).
The Septuagint adds, “A child who is taught will become wise and will make a fool his servant.”
Or “but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.” The same line appears in verse 11.
The second line repeats verse 8b. The Septuagint says, “but a person who corrects boldly makes peace.”
Or “and he adds no sorrow to it.”

verses.text:
Yahweh is disgusted by cheating scales,
but he is pleased by an accurate weight.{a}

Pride arrives, and shame follows close behind.
Wisdom stays with the humble.

Honesty guides decent people.
Crooked dealing destroys the unfaithful.

Money cannot help on the day of judgment,
but doing right saves a life from death.{b}

A blameless person’s goodness keeps his road straight,
but the wicked trip over their own evil.

The goodness of honest people sets them free,
but the unfaithful get caught by their own greed.

When a wicked person dies, his hope dies with him.
What he expected from his power is lost.{c}

A good person is pulled out of trouble,
and a wicked one steps into it instead.

A godless person ruins his neighbor with words,
but good people escape through what they know.

When good people succeed, the whole city celebrates.
When the wicked die, people cheer.

A city is lifted up by the blessing of honest people.
The words of the wicked pull it to the ground.

Putting down your neighbor shows a lack of sense.
A person with understanding keeps quiet.

A gossip wanders about telling secrets.
A trustworthy person keeps things private.

A nation with no direction collapses.
With many advisers, it is safe.

Anyone who guarantees a stranger’s loan will be hurt.
Anyone who refuses such deals stays safe.

A kind woman earns respect.
Ruthless men gather wealth.{d}

A merciful person does himself a favor.
A cruel person damages his own body.

The pay of a wicked person is an illusion.
The one who plants goodness gets a real reward.

Doing right leads firmly to life.
Chasing evil leads to death.

Yahweh is disgusted by twisted hearts,
but he is pleased with those whose lives are blameless.

You can be sure of this: the guilty will not escape punishment,
but the children of good people will go free.

A pig with a gold ring in its nose
is like a beautiful woman with no good sense.

Good people want only what is good.
The wicked can expect only anger.

One person gives freely and ends up with more.
Another saves too much and ends up poor.

Generous people will do well.
Those who bring others refreshment will find refreshment themselves.

People curse a man who hoards his grain,
but they bless the one who sells it.

Whoever searches for good finds approval.
Whoever goes looking for evil will have it find him.

Those who trust their money will fall,
but good people will thrive like green leaves.

Whoever brings trouble to his family will inherit only wind.
The fool will end up working for the wise.

The result of good living is a tree of life,
and a wise person wins others over.{e}

If good people are paid back on earth,
how much more the wicked and the sinful!{f}

notes.text: Literally “a full stone.” Weights were stones that merchants carried in a bag.
The Septuagint does not have this verse.
Or “what he expected from his wealth.” The Hebrew is not certain.
The Septuagint makes this longer: “A kind wife brings glory to her husband, but a woman who hates what is right brings shame. Lazy people end up in need, but hard workers hold on to wealth.”
Or “takes lives.” The Septuagint says “but the lives of lawbreakers are cut short.”
The Septuagint says, “If the righteous are barely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner be seen?” This is the form quoted in 1 Peter 4:18.

verses.text:
Whoever loves to be corrected loves to learn.
Whoever hates a warning is stupid as an animal.

Yahweh approves of a good person,
but he condemns anyone who makes sneaky plans.

Evil never makes a person secure,
but the roots of good people will not be pulled up.

A strong wife is a crown to her husband.
A wife who shames him is like rot in his bones.

Good people make fair plans.
The wicked give deceitful advice.

The words of the wicked wait like hunters to spill blood.
The words of honest people save lives.

Knock down the wicked and they are gone,
but the family of good people stays standing.

People praise someone for having good sense.
They look down on someone with a warped mind.

It is better to be ordinary and have a servant
than to act important and go without food.

A good person knows what his animals need.
Even the mercy of the wicked has cruelty in it.

Those who farm their land will have plenty to eat.
Those who chase empty dreams lack sense.{a}

The wicked want what crooks have caught.
The roots of good people bear fruit.{b}

An evil trap is set by a sinful tongue,
but a good person gets out of trouble.{c}

A person’s words bring good things to eat,
and the work of his hands comes back to reward him.

Fools think their own way is right.
Wise people take advice.

A fool shows his anger right away.
A sensible person shrugs off an insult.

An honest witness tells what is right.
A lying witness tells what cheats.

Thoughtless words cut like swords,
but wise people’s words bring healing.

Honest words last forever.
A lying tongue lasts a moment.

Deceit fills the minds of those who plot evil,
while those who work for peace have joy.

Nothing bad happens to good people,
but the wicked have trouble piled up.

Yahweh is disgusted by lying lips,
but he enjoys people who keep their word.

A clever person keeps his knowledge to himself.
A foolish heart blurts out its foolishness.

Hard workers will be in charge.
Lazy people will be put to forced labor.

Worry weighs a person down,
but a kind word lifts him up.

A good person gives guidance to a friend.{d}
The way of the wicked leads them off track.

A lazy person does not cook what he hunts,
but a hard worker holds valuable treasure.{e}

Life is found on the path of goodness.
Along that road there is no death.{f}

notes.text: The Septuagint adds, “Whoever enjoys banquets of wine will leave shame in his own fortress.”
The Hebrew of this verse is hard to read.
The Septuagint adds, “A person with a gentle look will be pitied, but one who fights at the gates hurts souls.”
Or “A good person looks for his own pasture.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
The Hebrew of this verse is hard to read.
Or “but the road of that path leads to death,” following some old copies.

verses.text:
A wise child takes a father’s training to heart,
but a mocker pays no attention to a warning.

Good words feed a person well,
but the unfaithful have an appetite for violence.

Guarding your mouth protects your life.
Talking without thinking leads to ruin.

The lazy want everything and get nothing,
but hard workers are fully satisfied.

Good people hate lies.
The wicked bring a stink and a shame.

Doing right protects the person who is honest,
and doing wrong knocks down the sinner.{a}

One person acts rich and has nothing.
Another acts poor and has a fortune.

A wealthy man may buy back his life with a payment,
but nobody even threatens a poor man.

The light of good people glows bright,
but the lamp of the wicked is put out.{b}

Pride produces only fights,
but wisdom comes to those who take advice.

Money earned in an empty way dwindles,
but money saved bit by bit grows.

When hope is put off too long, the heart gets sick.
When a wish comes true, it is like a tree of life.

Whoever laughs at instruction will pay the price.
Whoever honors a command will be given a reward.{c}

The teaching of wise people is a spring of life.
It helps you avoid the traps of death.

Good sense wins approval,
but the road of the unfaithful is rough.{d}

Every sensible person acts with knowledge,
but a fool displays his foolishness.

A wicked messenger lands in trouble,
but a reliable one brings healing.

Whoever ignores correction ends up poor and ashamed.
Whoever welcomes it is honored.

A wish come true is sweet to the soul,
but fools refuse to leave evil behind.

Walk with wise people and you will become wise.
Befriend fools and you will be hurt.

Trouble chases sinners,
but good people are repaid with good things.

Good people leave an inheritance for their grandchildren.
The property of sinners ends up with the just.

A poor person’s plowed ground may give plenty of food,
but injustice sweeps some of it away.{e}

Whoever will not discipline his child does not love him.
Whoever loves his child takes care to correct him.

Good people eat until they are full,
but the stomach of the wicked stays empty.

notes.text: The Septuagint does not have this verse.
The Septuagint adds, “Deceitful souls wander off into sins, but good people show pity and mercy.”
The Septuagint adds, “A deceitful child will have nothing good, but a wise servant will do well, and his way will be made straight.”
Or “lasts.” The Hebrew is uncertain. The Septuagint says “ends in destruction.”
The Hebrew of this verse is hard to read.

verses.text:
Wise women make their homes strong,{a}
but Folly tears her own down with her bare hands.

A person who lives honestly respects Yahweh.
A person with crooked ways despises him.

A fool’s talk is a stick that beats his own pride,{b}
but the speech of the wise protects them.

With no oxen, the feed box stays clean,
but a strong ox brings in a big harvest.

A truthful witness does not lie.
A false witness breathes out lies.

A mocker searches for wisdom and finds none.
For a person with understanding, knowledge comes easily.

Walk away from a fool.
You will not hear any knowledge on his lips.

The wisdom of a sensible person is to know where he is headed.
The foolishness of fools is cheating.

Fools laugh off their guilt,{c}
but honest people share good will.

Each heart knows its own bitter pain,
and no outsider can share its joy.

The home of the wicked will be destroyed,
but the tent of honest people will thrive.

One road seems right to a person,
yet it ends in death.

Even while laughing, a heart may ache,
and happiness can end in sadness.

Unfaithful people get all they deserve from their own paths.
Good people get what they deserve from theirs.{d}

A simple person believes anything.
A sensible person looks at each step.

A wise person is careful and avoids evil.
A fool is careless and feels sure of himself.

Someone with a short temper acts foolishly,
and a person who plots is hated.

Simple people are given foolishness as their inheritance.
Sensible people wear knowledge as a crown.

The evil will kneel before the good.
The wicked will stand waiting at the doors of the righteous.

Even his neighbor avoids a poor man,
but a rich man has friends by the dozen.

Looking down on a neighbor is a sin.
Happy is the person who shows kindness to the poor.

Surely those who plot evil go astray.
Those who plan good earn faithful love and trust.

All hard work brings a profit.
Mere talk brings only poverty.

Wealth is a crown for the wise.
The foolishness of fools stays foolishness.{e}

A truthful witness saves lives.
One who breathes out lies is a cheat.

Respect for Yahweh gives strong safety,
and it gives a refuge to a person’s children.

Respect for Yahweh is a spring of life.
It helps you dodge the traps of death.

A ruler gets glory from a large population.
Without subjects, a prince is ruined.

A patient person has great understanding.
A hothead shows off his foolishness.

A peaceful heart keeps the body alive,
but jealousy makes the bones rot.

Whoever crushes the poor insults the God who made them.
Whoever shows kindness to those in need gives God honor.

The wicked are knocked down by their own evil,
but good people find shelter even when they die.{f}

Wisdom rests quietly in the heart of a person with understanding,
but among fools she has to make herself known.{g}

Doing right lifts up a nation,
but sin brings shame on any people.

A king is pleased with a servant who acts wisely,
but his anger lands on one who brings shame.

notes.text: Or “Wisdom builds her house.” The plural form of the word wisdom can show honor, as in 9:1.
Or “a branch of pride.”
Or “Guilt laughs at fools.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
Or “and a good person gets satisfied from what he does.”
The Septuagint says, “The crown of wise people is a clever mind, but the work of fools is evil.”
Hebrew bemoto (“in his death”). Many scholars read betummo (“in his honesty”) by switching two letters. The Septuagint says “in his own holiness.”
The Septuagint and some other old copies say, “but in the heart of fools she is not known.”

verses.text:
Calm words cool down a rage,
but cutting words fire up anger.

Wise people make knowledge attractive when they speak.
Fools let foolishness bubble out.

Yahweh’s eyes are on every place,
watching both bad people and good.

Kind speech is a tree of life.
Twisted speech breaks a person’s spirit.

A fool rejects his father’s training.
Anyone who accepts correction shows good sense.

Great treasure fills the home of a good person,
but the income of the wicked brings trouble.

Wise lips spread knowledge around.
The hearts of fools do not.

Yahweh is disgusted by the offerings of the wicked,
but honest people’s prayers make him glad.

Yahweh hates the way the wicked live,
but he loves anyone who chases after what is right.

Cruel punishment waits for anyone who leaves the right road.
Anyone who hates correction will die.

Even the grave and the place of ruin{a} are open to Yahweh.
So human hearts are no secret to him!

A mocker hates being corrected.
He will not visit wise people.

A happy heart puts a smile on the face,
but a sad heart breaks the spirit.

A sensible mind goes after knowledge.
The mouth of a fool feeds on foolishness.

Every day is hard when you are poor,
but a cheerful heart is like a never-ending party.

A little with respect for Yahweh
beats a fortune with worry.

A plate of vegetables with love
is better than steak with hate.

A hothead starts fights.
A patient person ends them.{b}

The road of a lazy person is blocked with thorns.
The road of an honest person is a smooth highway.

A wise child makes a father happy,
but a foolish person looks down on his mother.

Foolishness makes people with no sense happy.
A person with understanding walks straight ahead.

Plans fail without advice.
With many advisers, they succeed.

People enjoy giving a fitting answer.
A word at just the right time is wonderful!

For the wise, the path of life goes up,
so they stay away from the grave below.

Yahweh knocks down the proud person’s house,
but he marks the border of the widow’s land.

Yahweh hates evil plans,
but kind words are clean in his sight.

Someone greedy for gain brings trouble to his family.
Someone who refuses bribes will live.{c}

Good people think before they reply.
The wicked pour out evil with their mouths.{d}

Yahweh stays far away from the wicked,
yet he hears the prayers of good people.{e}

A sparkle in the eyes makes the heart glad,
and good news puts strength in the body.

Anyone who listens to correction that gives life
will feel at home among wise people.{f}

Ignoring instruction means throwing your life away.
Listening to a warning builds good sense.

Respect for Yahweh teaches wisdom,
and humility comes before honor.

notes.text: Hebrew Abaddon, “destruction.” It is another name for the place of the dead, paired with Sheol.
The Septuagint adds, “A person who is slow to anger puts out arguments, but a godless person stirs them up.”
The Septuagint adds, “Giving to the poor and dealing faithfully wash sins away. Respect for the Lord makes everyone turn from evil.” This is a form of 16:6.
The Septuagint adds, “The ways of good people are acceptable to the Lord, and even enemies become friends through them.” This is a form of 16:7.
The Septuagint adds, “A small income with justice is better than large crops with injustice. Let a person’s heart think rightly, so that God will straighten his steps.” These are forms of 16:8–9.
The Septuagint does not have this verse.

verses.text:
People make plans in their hearts,
but the right words to say come from Yahweh.{a}

To himself, everyone’s behavior looks clean,
but Yahweh tests what is inside.

Hand your work over to Yahweh,
and your plans will succeed.

Yahweh made everything with a purpose,
even the wicked, who are meant for the day of trouble.

Yahweh is disgusted by every proud heart.
Be certain that none of them will escape punishment.

Faithful love and truth wipe away guilt,
and respect for Yahweh keeps people from evil.

When Yahweh is pleased with how someone lives,
he can even make that person’s enemies friendly.

A small income earned honestly
is better than a large one earned unfairly.

A person’s mind designs his course,
but Yahweh decides where he steps.

A king speaks with the voice of a judge.
He must not make unfair rulings.

Yahweh owns honest scales and balances.
He made every weight in the bag.

Kings hate wrongdoing,
because a throne stands firm on what is right.

Kings like to hear honest speech.
They love anyone who speaks the truth.

A king’s anger can mean a death sentence,
but a wise person can calm it down.

A king’s smiling face means life.
His favor is like a spring rain cloud.

How much better to get wisdom than gold!
Choosing understanding beats choosing silver.

The road of honest people curves away from evil.
Whoever watches the road protects his life.

Pride comes right before a crash.
A stuck-up attitude comes before a tumble.

Better to be low and humble among the poor
than to split stolen goods with the proud.

Anyone who thinks about a matter carefully will do well.
Whoever trusts Yahweh is blessed.

A wise heart earns the name “understanding.”
Pleasant words make teaching more convincing.

Understanding is a spring of life for the one who has it,
but fools are punished by their own foolishness.

A wise heart guides what the mouth says
and makes the lips more convincing.

Kind words are like honey from the comb.
They are sweet to the soul and healthy for the body.

One road seems right to a person,
yet it ends in death.

A worker’s hunger works for him,
because his stomach pushes him to keep going.

A worthless person digs up trouble.
His speech burns like fire.

A twisted person spreads fighting,
and a gossip splits up close friends.

A violent person lures his neighbor
onto a road that is not good.

One who winks is planning something crooked.
One who bites his lips has already done the harm.

Gray hair is a glorious crown.
It is earned by living right.

Patience is stronger than a soldier.
Self-control is worth more than conquering a city.

People throw dice to decide,
but every outcome comes from Yahweh.

notes.text: The Septuagint does not have verses 1, 3, 4, and 6 in this form. Forms of verses 6–9 also appear at the end of chapter 15.

verses.text:
A dry piece of bread eaten in peace
is better than a home packed with feast food{a} and fighting.

A sensible servant will take charge over a child who brings shame,
and will share the family property with the other sons.

Silver is tested in a pot and gold in a furnace,
but Yahweh is the one who tests hearts.

An evildoer pays close attention to wicked talk.
A liar listens to a destructive tongue.

Whoever makes fun of poor people insults their Maker.
Anyone who gloats over a disaster will be punished.

Grandchildren are a crown for the aged,
and children take pride in their parents.{b}

Fancy words do not fit a fool,
and lies fit a leader even less.

To the person who gives it, a bribe looks like a magic charm.
It seems to work wherever he turns.

Whoever forgives a wrong builds friendship.
Whoever keeps bringing it up pulls close friends apart.

One word of correction sinks deeper into a person with understanding
than a hundred whips into a fool.

An evil person wants nothing but revolt,
so a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

Better to run into a mother bear whose cubs were stolen
than to meet a fool who is acting foolish.

If anyone returns evil for good,
evil will never leave his home.

The start of a fight is like a crack in a dam.
Quit before the quarrel bursts out.

Letting the guilty go free and punishing the innocent:
Yahweh hates them both.

What use is money in a fool’s hand?
He wants to buy wisdom but has no mind to learn it.{c}

A friend loves at every moment.
A brother is born to help in hard times.

A person with no sense shakes hands on a deal
and promises to cover a neighbor’s debt.

Anyone who loves sin loves fighting.
Whoever makes his doorway tall is begging for a crash.

A twisted heart finds nothing good.
A deceitful tongue lands in trouble.

Having a fool for a child brings sorrow.
The father of a dull person has no joy.

A cheerful heart works like good medicine,
but a crushed spirit saps strength.

A wicked person slips a bribe out of his clothing{d}
to twist the course of justice.

A person with understanding keeps wisdom in front of him,
but a fool’s eyes wander to the far ends of the earth.

A foolish child brings grief to his father
and bitter pain to the mother who bore him.

It is not good to fine an innocent person,
or to flog leaders because they were honest.

Whoever uses few words has knowledge.
A person with a cool temper has understanding.

Even fools seem wise if they stay quiet.
They seem smart if they keep their mouths closed.

notes.text: Literally “sacrifices.” People ate the meat at sacrifice meals.
The Septuagint adds, “The faithful own a whole world of wealth, but the unfaithful do not own a single coin.”
The Septuagint adds, “Whoever builds his house high is looking for ruin. Whoever turns away from learning will fall into trouble.”
Literally “from the chest,” meaning from a fold in his clothing.

verses.text:
A loner chases his own wishes.
He lashes out at every piece of good advice.{a}

A fool does not enjoy understanding.
He only enjoys sharing his own opinions.

When the wicked come, scorn comes too,
and shame brings insults.

The words from a person’s mouth are deep water.
The source of wisdom is a rushing stream.

It is wrong to take the side of a guilty person
or to deny justice to the innocent in court.

A fool’s words walk him into a fight.
His mouth is asking for a beating.

A fool’s mouth is what ruins him.
His lips are a trap for his own life.

A gossip’s words are like delicious snacks.
They sink deep into a person’s insides.

Anyone who is lazy at work
is a close relative of someone who wrecks things.

The name of Yahweh is a strong tower.
Good people run into it and are safe.

A rich person thinks his wealth is a strong city.
In his mind it is a tall wall.

A heart grows proud just before a fall,
and humility comes before honor.

Replying before you have listened
is foolish and shameful.

A strong spirit can get a person through illness,
but who can bear a broken spirit?

A mind with understanding gains knowledge,
and the ears of the wise go looking for it.

A gift can open doors for a person
and bring him in front of important people.

The first person to tell his side sounds right
until the other comes and asks questions.

Drawing lots ends arguments
and settles things between strong rivals.

A brother who has been hurt is tougher to win back than a walled city.
Arguments are like the bars on a fortress gate.{b}

A person’s stomach is filled by what his mouth says.
He is satisfied with the harvest of his lips.

Life and death are in the tongue’s power.
Those who enjoy talking will eat the crop it grows.

A man who finds a wife has found something good,
and he has gained Yahweh’s favor.{c}

A poor man begs for mercy,
but a rich man answers with harsh words.{d}

A person with many friends may be ruined,
but some friends stick closer than family.

notes.text: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
The Hebrew of this verse is hard to read.
The Septuagint adds, “Whoever sends away a good wife sends away something good. Whoever keeps an unfaithful wife is foolish and ungodly.”
The Septuagint does not have verses 23–24 and 19:1–2.

verses.text:
A poor person who lives honestly
is better off than a fool who speaks crookedly.

Eagerness without knowledge is not good.
Rushing along makes a person miss the turn.

A person’s own foolishness ruins his life,
and then his heart is angry at Yahweh.

Money brings in lots of friends,
but a poor person’s friend walks away.

A lying witness will be found guilty.
One who breathes out lies will not get off.

Many people try to win a generous person’s favor,
and everybody is a friend to one who gives gifts.

Whoever gains good sense loves his own life.
Whoever holds on to understanding will find success.

A lying witness will be found guilty.
One who breathes out lies will be destroyed.

A life of luxury is not right for a fool,
and it is worse for a slave to rule over princes.

Good sense helps a person stay patient,
and overlooking an insult is to his credit.

A king’s rage sounds like a lion roaring,
but his approval is as refreshing as morning dew on grass.

A foolish son is a disaster for his father.
A wife who nags is like a leaky roof that never stops dripping.

Parents leave behind houses and money,
but a sensible wife is a gift from Yahweh.

Laziness brings on deep sleep,
and a person who does nothing goes hungry.

Whoever follows the command protects his life.
Whoever is careless about how he lives will die.

Whoever is kind to the poor is making Yahweh a loan,
and Yahweh will pay him back for it.

Discipline your child while there is hope,
and never aim at his destruction.{b}

A hothead will have to pay the penalty.
Save him once, and you will be doing it over and over.

Listen to advice and accept correction,
so that you will be wise later in life.

A person’s heart holds many plans,
but only Yahweh’s purpose will stand.

What people want from others is faithful love,{c}
and being poor is better than being a liar.

Respect for Yahweh leads to life.
A person who has it rests easy, and harm does not touch him.

The lazy person reaches into the bowl
but is too weary to lift food to his mouth.

Beat a mocker, and the simple will gain some sense.
Correct an understanding person, and he will learn more.

Whoever steals from his father and throws out his mother
is a child who causes shame and disgrace.

My child, if you quit hearing correction,
you will wander off from the things you know.

A worthless witness makes fun of justice,
and the mouth of the wicked gulps down evil.

Punishments are ready for mockers,
and whips for the backs of fools.

notes.text: The third line is uncertain. It may be a piece of a lost saying. The Septuagint has a longer text here.
Or “do not wish for his death,” meaning do not discipline him in a rage. Or “do not be set on ruining him” by neglecting him.
Or “A person’s greed is his shame.”

verses.text:
Wine makes people mock, and beer makes them brawl.
No one who is fooled by them is wise.

A king’s rage roars like a young lion.
Whoever makes him angry risks his life.

Staying out of fights brings honor to a person,
but every fool is quick to quarrel.

A lazy farmer will not plow in the fall.
At harvest he looks for a crop and finds none.

Plans inside a person are like deep water in a well,
but someone with insight can draw them out.

Plenty of people boast about their loyalty,
but who can find a person who is truly reliable?

A good person lives honestly.
His children are blessed after him!

A king sitting on his judge’s throne
separates out all evil with a look.

Who can say, “I have cleaned up my heart.
I am free from my sin”?{a}

Using one weight to buy and another to sell, or two sizes of measuring cup,{b}
is something Yahweh hates.

Even a child shows by his actions
whether his behavior is clean and honest.

Hearing ears and seeing eyes
were both made by Yahweh.

Do not fall in love with sleep, or poverty will find you.
Keep your eyes open and you will have food to spare.

“It is no good, no good,” says the buyer.
Then he walks off and brags about the deal.{c}

Gold and jewels are easy to find,
but lips that speak with knowledge are a rare treasure.

Take the coat of a man who promised to cover a stranger’s debt.
Keep it as a deposit if he backs a foreign woman’s loan.{d}

Food won by cheating tastes sweet at first,
but later the mouth is full of gravel.

Plans succeed when people get advice.
Fight a war only with good direction.

A gossip goes around telling secrets,
so stay away from a person who talks too much.

People who insult their father or mother
will see their lamp snuffed out in pitch darkness.

Property grabbed quickly at the start
will not be blessed in the end.

Do not announce, “I will repay that wrong myself.”
Wait for Yahweh, and he will rescue you.

Yahweh hates it when people use two different weights,
and cheating scales are wrong.

Yahweh directs a person’s steps.
So how can anyone understand his own road?

It is a trap to promise something to God in a rush
and think about the promise only afterward.

A wise king separates out the wicked
and rolls the threshing wheel across them.

The human spirit is a lamp from Yahweh.
It shines into every hidden part of a person.

Faithful love and truth protect a king,
and love keeps his throne steady.

Young men are proud of their strength,
and old men are honored for their gray hair.

Wounds that hurt can scrub out evil,
and a beating goes deep inside a person.

notes.text: In the Septuagint, verses 20–22 come here, and verses 14–19 are missing.
Literally “a stone and a stone, an ephah and an ephah.” This means one set of weights and measures for buying and another for selling. An ephah was a dry measure of about 3/5 bushel (22 liters).
The Septuagint does not have verses 14–19.
Or “a foreigner,” following another way of reading the Hebrew. Compare 27:13.

verses.text:
A king’s heart is like a canal in Yahweh’s hand.
He steers it wherever he wants.

People think every path they take is right,
but Yahweh checks their hearts.

Yahweh would rather see people do what is right and fair
than bring him sacrifices.

Proud eyes and a boastful heart
are the lamp of the wicked, and they are sin.{a}

The plans of hard workers lead to gain,
but everyone who rushes ends up in need.{b}

Wealth earned with a lying tongue
is a puff of smoke and a deadly trap.{c}

The wicked will be swept off by their own violence,
since they will not deal fairly.

A guilty person’s road is crooked,
but the actions of a clean person are straight.

Living in the corner of an attic roof
beats sharing a home with a quarrelsome wife.

The wicked person craves evil.
His neighbor gets no mercy from him.

When a mocker is punished, simple people learn wisdom.
When a wise person receives teaching, his knowledge grows.

The Righteous One{d} sees into the home of the wicked
and throws them down into ruin.

If you plug your ears when the poor cry out,
you will cry out someday and get no answer.

A secret gift calms anger,
and a bribe tucked in a coat cools a rage.

Justice makes good people glad
and makes evildoers afraid.

Anyone who wanders from the road of understanding
will rest among the ghosts of the dead.

Those who chase pleasure will end up poor.
Those who love wine and rich food will never get wealthy.

The wicked are the price paid to free the good,
and the faithless are paid for the honest.

Living out in the wilderness
is better than living with a nagging, angry wife.

Treasure and oil are stored in a wise person’s home,
but a fool gulps them all down.

Anyone who chases goodness and faithful love
finds life, justice, and honor.

A wise person can march against a city full of fighters
and pull down the fortress they trusted in.

Guard your mouth and tongue,
and you will keep yourself out of trouble.

A proud and arrogant person is called a “mocker.”
He acts with fierce pride.

The lazy person’s cravings will kill him,
because his hands will not work.

All day long he wants more,
but a good person gives without holding back.

The wicked person’s offering is disgusting.
It is even worse when he brings it with bad motives!

A lying witness will die,
but one who listens will keep on speaking.{e}

A wicked person puts on a hard face.
An honest person thinks about where his road goes.{f}

No wisdom, no understanding,
and no plan can win against Yahweh.

Soldiers prepare their horses for the battle,
but Yahweh alone gives the win.

notes.text: Or “the farm of the wicked.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
The Septuagint does not have this verse.
This follows the Septuagint and some other old copies. The Hebrew says “for those who seek death.”
Or “A righteous person.” The second line suggests it means God.
Or “will speak and win.” The meaning is uncertain.
This follows the margin of the Hebrew text. The written text says “understands his ways.”

verses.text:
A good reputation beats enormous riches.
Being admired is worth more than silver or gold.

Rich and poor share one thing:
Yahweh made every one of them.

A sensible person sees danger and hides,
but simple people walk on and suffer for it.

The prize for humility and respect for Yahweh
is wealth, honor, and life.

Thorns and traps lie on the roads of crooked people.
Whoever protects his life stays far away from them.

Teach a child the way that fits him,
and even when he is old he will not leave it.{a}

The rich boss around the poor,
and a borrower is a servant to the lender.

Whoever plants injustice will harvest trouble,
and the stick of his anger will break.{b}

Kind people will receive blessings,
since they hand some of their food to the poor.{c}

Throw out the mocker and the fighting leaves with him.
Arguments and insults end.

Anyone who loves purity of heart and has gracious words
becomes a friend of the king.

Yahweh’s eyes guard those who have knowledge,
but he ruins the words of the unfaithful.

Someone lazy makes excuses: “There is a lion out there!
I would be killed in the street!”

The mouth of an unfaithful woman is a deep pit.
Anyone Yahweh is angry with will fall in.{d}

Foolishness is tied up in the heart of a child.
The stick of correction will drive it far away.

Squeezing the poor to get rich,
and giving gifts to the rich: both lead to poverty.

Lean in and hear the words of wise people,{e}
and turn your mind to my knowledge.

It will be a pleasure to keep them inside you
and to have them all ready to say.

I am teaching them to you today, to you personally,
so that you will put your trust in Yahweh.

I have written you thirty sayings{f}
full of advice and knowledge.

They show what is right and true, words you can count on,
so you can send back honest answers to those who sent you.

Never steal from poor people just because they are poor.
Never crush those in need at the city gate.

Yahweh will take up their case
and take the life of anyone who has robbed them.

Never become a friend of a person with a quick temper.
Never travel with someone full of rage.

If you do, you will pick up his habits
and be caught in a trap.

Do not be one of those who shake hands on a deal
and promise to pay another person’s debts.

If you have no money to pay,
why should your own bed be taken from under you?

Do not move the old boundary stone
that your ancestors put in place.

Do you see someone who is skilled and quick at his work?
He will serve kings.
He will not serve unimportant people.

notes.text: Or “according to the way he should go.” The Septuagint does not have this verse.
The Septuagint adds, “God loves a cheerful, generous giver, but he will bring the empty work of the stingy to an end.” Compare 2 Corinthians 9:7.
The Septuagint adds, “Whoever gives freely wins victory and honor, but he takes away the life of those who keep the gifts for themselves.”
The Septuagint adds, “Evil ways lie in front of a person, and he does not like to turn away from them. But he must turn aside from a twisted and evil way.”
A new collection starts here (22:17–24:22). It is very close to the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope, which has thirty chapters.
The Hebrew text has the word shilshom (“before”), but the margin has shalishim. Many readers take it as “thirty” or as “excellent things.” The Septuagint says “write them three times.”

subheads.24: Do Not Befriend an Angry Man

verses.text:
When you sit down to dine with a powerful person,
look carefully at what{a} is placed in front of you.

If you tend to overeat,
imagine a knife at your throat.

Do not crave his fancy foods.
That meal is a trick.

Do not wear yourself out chasing money.
Be wise enough to quit.

You glance at it, and it vanishes.
Money sprouts wings
and soars off like an eagle.

Never eat at the table of a selfish person.{b}
Never crave his tasty treats.

You will throw up the little you ate,
and your kind words will go to waste.

Do not speak your best advice to a fool.
He will sneer at your wise words.

Do not move the old boundary stone.
Do not take over the fields of orphans.

Their Defender{d} is strong.
He will argue their case against you.

Give your mind to instruction.
Give your ears to words of knowledge.

Do not hold back correction from a child.
A spanking will not kill him.

Use the stick on him yourself,
and you will save his life from the grave.

My child, if your mind is wise,
my own heart will celebrate too.

My insides{e} will cheer
when your lips say what is right.

Do not let your heart envy sinners.
Keep respecting Yahweh every day.

There is certainly a future for you,
and your hope will not be wiped out.

Listen, my child, and be wise.
Point your heart in the right direction.

Do not join those who drink too much wine
or stuff themselves with meat.

Drunks and big eaters will become poor,
and sleepiness will put them in rags.

Listen to your father, who gave you life.
Do not look down on your mother when she grows old.

Buy truth and never sell it.
Buy wisdom, training, and understanding too.

The father of a good child will shout for joy.
The parent of a wise child will be delighted.

Make your father and mother happy.
Give joy to the woman who gave birth to you.

My child, hand your heart over to me.
Let your eyes enjoy{f} my ways.

A woman who sells herself is a deep ditch.
An unfaithful wife is a narrow well.

She waits like a thief
and adds to the number of the unfaithful.

Who groans? Who is full of sorrow?
Who gets into fights? Who complains?
Who has cuts and bruises with no cause?
Who has bloodshot eyes?

Those who stay up late with their wine,
who go looking for mixed drinks.

Do not stare at wine that is red,
that sparkles in the cup
and slides down easily.

Later it bites like a snake
and spits poison like a viper.

Your eyes will see strange things,
and your mouth will say twisted things.

You will feel like you are lying in the middle of the ocean,
or like you are sleeping at the top of a ship’s mast.{g}

“They hit me,” you say, “but I felt nothing.
They beat me up, and I did not notice.
When will I wake up?
I want another drink.”

notes.text: Or “who.”
Literally “of someone with an evil eye.”
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. It may also mean “as he figures in his soul, so he is.”
Hebrew go’el, the close relative who protects the rights of a family member. Here it means God himself.
Literally “my kidneys,” which people thought of as the place of deep feelings.
This follows the written Hebrew text. The margin says “keep.”
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.

subheads.6: Do Not Trust a Stingy Host
subheads.12: Learn and Make Your Parents Proud

verses.text:
Do not envy wicked people.
Do not wish to be with them.

Their hearts dream up violence,
and their mouths talk of causing trouble.

A house is built with wisdom,
and understanding makes it strong.

Knowledge fills its rooms
with all kinds of rare and lovely treasures.

A wise person has strength,{a}
and a person with knowledge grows more powerful.

You need good direction to fight a war,
and victory comes with many advisers.

Wisdom is too high for fools.
At the town gate, they keep their mouths shut.

Anyone who plans to do wrong
will be known as a schemer.

Planning foolish things is a sin,
and people cannot stand a mocker.

If you give up when trouble comes,
you were not very strong.

Save those who are being dragged off to die.
Hold back those who are stumbling toward slaughter.

Suppose you say, “We did not know about this.”
Does the one who weighs hearts not notice?
Does the one who watches over you not know?
Will he not pay each person back for what he did?

Have some honey, my child, since it is good.
Drops from the honeycomb taste sweet.

Wisdom is just as sweet to your soul.
Find it, and your future is secure,
and your hope will not be cut short.

Wicked person, do not lurk near a good person’s home.
Do not wreck his place of rest.

A good person may fall seven times and get back up,
but the wicked are knocked down by disaster.

Do not cheer when your enemy falls.
Do not feel glad when he stumbles.

Yahweh might see it and be displeased,
and then turn his anger away from that man.

Do not get upset over evildoers.
Do not envy the wicked.

Evildoers have no future ahead.
The wicked person’s lamp will be put out.

My child, respect Yahweh and the king.
Do not join people who like to change sides,{b}

because disaster from them will come without warning.
Who knows what ruin they can both bring?{c}

Here are more sayings of the wise:{d}
Taking sides when you judge is wrong.

Whoever says to a guilty person, “You are in the clear,”
will be cursed by many peoples and hated by nations.

But those who judge the guilty fairly will be glad,
and great blessings will rest on them.

An honest answer
is like a friendly kiss on the lips.

Finish your outdoor work first.
Get your fields in shape,
and only after that build your house.

Never speak against your neighbor without cause.
Would you deceive with your words?

Do not say, “I will treat him the way he treated me.
I will get him back for what he did.”

I walked past the field of a lazy person,
past the vineyard of a man with no sense.

Thistles had taken over the whole place.
Weeds covered the ground,
and the stone wall had fallen down.

I looked at it and thought it over.
I saw it and took the lesson to heart:

a little sleep, a short nap,
a bit of folding the arms to rest,

and poverty will come at you like a robber,
and need will come like a man with a weapon.{e}

notes.text: This follows the Septuagint and some other old copies. The Hebrew says “A wise man is in strength.”
Or “with people of high rank.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
The Septuagint adds a long passage here on the son who keeps the command and on the king’s tongue as a sword. In the Septuagint, 30:1–14 also comes here.
A short collection starts here (24:23–34).
In the Septuagint, 30:15–33 and 31:1–9 come after this verse. Then chapters 25–29 follow, and then 31:10–31.

subheads.30: A Lesson from a Lazy Man’s Field

verses.text: These are more proverbs of Solomon. The officials of King Hezekiah{a} of Judah copied them out.

God gets glory for hiding things.
Kings get glory for searching things out.

The sky is high and the earth is deep.
A king’s mind cannot be figured out.

Remove the waste from silver,
and the silversmith can make a vessel.

Remove the wicked from the king’s presence,
and his throne will stand firm because of what is right.

Do not brag in front of the king.
Do not stand where important people stand.

Do not hurry to take a quarrel to court.
What will you do in the end
if your neighbor proves you wrong?

Settle the matter with your neighbor directly.
Do not give away someone else’s secret.

Otherwise, whoever hears it may blame you,
and you will never lose your bad name.{c}

A word spoken at the right moment
is like gold apples in a silver bowl.{d}

A wise person’s correction to a listening ear
is like a gold ring or a fine gold necklace.

A trustworthy messenger is like cold snow in the heat of harvest
to those who send him.
He gives his master new strength.

Clouds and wind without rain:
that is a person who brags about a gift he never gives.

With patience you can persuade a ruler,
and a gentle tongue can crush a bone.

Found some honey? Take just your share.
Too much will make you sick.

Do not visit your neighbor’s house too often,
or he will get tired of you and hate you.

Someone who tells lies about his neighbor in court
is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.

Trusting a traitor in a time of trouble
is like a rotten tooth or a foot that slips.

Singing songs to a sad heart is like taking off a coat in cold weather,
or like pouring vinegar on soda.{e} {f}

Is your enemy hungry? Feed him.
Is he thirsty? Give him a drink.

You will be stacking glowing coals on his head,{g}
and Yahweh will pay you back with good.

The north wind brings rain,
and secret talk brings angry looks.{h}

Living in the corner of an attic roof
beats sharing a home with a quarrelsome wife.

Good news from far away
is like cold water for a thirsty throat.

A good person who gives way to the wicked
is like a muddy spring or a dirty well.

Eating too much honey is not good,
and neither is chasing your own praise.{i}

A person with no self-control
is like a city with its walls knocked down.

notes.text: Hezekiah means “Yahweh makes strong.” He was king of Judah from about 715 to 686 BC (2 Kings 18–20).
The last line may belong with verse 8.
The Septuagint adds, “Kindness and friendship set a person free. Keep them for yourself so you do not become a target of blame, and guard your ways in peace.”
The meaning of the Hebrew word for “bowl” is uncertain. It may mean “carvings.”
Hebrew nether, a natural soda that fizzes when vinegar is poured on it.
The Septuagint adds, “As a moth harms clothing and a worm harms wood, so a person’s grief harms the heart.”
This picture means making him burn with shame. It may come from an Egyptian ceremony of being sorry. It is quoted in Romans 12:20.
Rain in Israel mostly comes from the west. So “north” may mean “northwest,” or the saying may come from another place.
The second line is uncertain. It could also mean “but searching out hard things is glory.”

verses.text:
Snow in summer and rain at harvest
do not fit, and neither does honor for a fool.

A fluttering sparrow and a darting swallow
do not land. A curse with no cause does not land either.{a}

Horses need whips, donkeys need bridles,
and fools need a stick on the back.

Do not answer a fool with his own kind of foolishness,
or you will turn into a fool too.

Answer a fool with his own kind of foolishness,
or he will think he is wise.{b}

Sending a message with a fool
is like chopping off your own feet and drinking trouble.

A proverb in a fool’s mouth
hangs as limp as the legs of a lame man.

Honoring a fool
is like tying a stone into a sling.

A proverb in a fool’s mouth
is like a thorn bush in the hand of a drunk.

Someone who hires a fool, or anyone who happens to pass by,
is like an archer who wounds everyone.{c}

A dog goes back to what it threw up.
A fool does his foolish thing again.{d}

Do you see a person who thinks he is wise?
A fool has more hope than he does.

The lazy person says, “There is a lion on the road!
A lion is roaming the squares!”

A door swings back and forth on its hinges,
and a lazy person rolls over in bed.

The lazy person digs his hand into the dish
and is too tired to lift it up to his mouth.

A lazy person believes he is smarter
than seven people who give sensible answers.

Grabbing a stray dog by the ears
is like jumping into a fight that is not yours.

A crazy person might shoot flaming sticks,
arrows, and death.

One who tricks his neighbor
and then says, “I was only joking!” is no better.

Without wood, a fire goes out.
Without a gossip, a fight dies down.

Charcoal keeps embers glowing, and wood keeps a fire going.
A quarrelsome person keeps fights burning the same way.

A gossip’s words are like delicious snacks.
They go deep into a person’s insides.

Sweet talk from an evil heart
is like shiny glaze brushed over a clay pot.{e}

A hateful person hides it with his speech,
but inside he stores up lies.

When he talks kindly, do not trust him,
because seven disgusting things fill his heart.

His hatred may be covered up with tricks,
but his evil will be shown to the whole community.

Anyone who digs a pit will land in it.
Anyone who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.

A lying tongue hates the people it hurts,
and flattering talk causes ruin.

notes.text: This follows the margin of the Hebrew text. The written text says “does not come to it,” which may mean “does not come to the one who spoke it.”
Verses 4 and 5 sit side by side on purpose. Whether to answer a fool depends on the situation.
This verse is very hard to understand in Hebrew. Another suggestion is, “A master worker makes everything, but a person who hires a fool is like one who hires anyone who passes by.”
Quoted in 2 Peter 2:22. The Septuagint adds, “There is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that is glory and kindness.”
Or, by changing the Hebrew slightly, “like glaze over clay.” A word from the Ugaritic language suggests that “silver waste” should be read as “glaze.”

verses.text:
Do not boast about what tomorrow will bring.
You cannot know what a single day may produce.

Let someone else say good things about you, not your own mouth.
Let a stranger do it, not your own lips.

Stone is heavy and sand is a load,
but a fool’s annoying ways weigh more than both.

Rage is cruel, and anger floods everything,
but who can stand up to jealousy?

An honest warning out loud
is better than love that stays hidden.

A friend’s wounds can be trusted,
but an enemy’s kisses are too many to count.{a}

A person who is full will turn down even honey,
but to a hungry person every bitter thing tastes sweet.

Someone who strays far from home
is like a bird that strays far from its nest.

Perfume and incense make the heart glad,
and so does a friend’s sweet advice from the heart.{b}

Stay loyal to your own friend and to your father’s friend.
When disaster hits, do not rush to a brother’s house.
Someone living close by helps more than a brother who lives far off.

Be wise, my child, and bring joy to my heart.
Then I can reply to anyone who ridicules me.

A sensible person sees danger and hides.
Simple people keep walking and suffer for it.
